prompt: A `/srv/www/default/html/restricted/.htaccess` contains `AuthType Basic`, `AuthUserFile /srv/www/security/site-passwd`, `AuthName Restricted`, `Require valid-user`, `Order deny,allow`, `Deny from all`, `Allow from 10.1.2.0/24`, `Satisfy any`; `DocumentRoot` is `/srv/www/default/html`. Select the two true statements.
choices: Clients on the `10.1.2.0/24` network will not need to authenticate to access `http://server/restricted/`
Apache grants access only to authenticated users connecting from `10.1.2.0/24`
This works only if `/srv/www/default/html/restricted/` is configured with `AllowOverride AuthConfig Limit`
The `Satisfy` directive can be removed without changing Apache's behavior for this directory
Apache requires authentication for every client requesting `http://server/restricted/`
explanation: `Satisfy any` means meeting either the host rule (`Allow from 10.1.2.0/24`) or the user rule is sufficient, so clients on that network skip authentication. The `.htaccess` only takes effect if the directory permits `AllowOverride AuthConfig Limit`.
